reuse.why: Builds on the existing getRangeExpectedAmount and the shared getApproxNumberThreshold tolerance, but adds getExpectedAmount next to the existing getScheduledAmount instead of extending it.

duplication.why: getExpectedAmount repeats getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own dispatch wrapped around the new helper.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and reuses the tolerance from shared/rules.ts, matching where amount rules already live.

scope.why: Only the expected-amount sites, a focused test and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: Two parallel resolvers (getExpectedAmount on the server, getScheduledAmount for the client) and a preview site that short-circuits numbers mean approximate amounts resolve differently depending on the path.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps `typeof schedule._amount === 'number' ? schedule._amount : getExpectedAmount(...)`, so its numeric branch bypasses the new rule; getScheduledAmount is left as a separate, unchanged resolver.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount is getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch reshaped (operator added, inverse dropped) rather than a single extended function.

one_place.where: getExpectedAmount holds the rule for api-models, schedule-template, forecast and schedules/app, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still decides numeric amounts itself and getScheduledAmount (used by the client) does not apply the approximate rule.
